title: Impacts of producing goods
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:15Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: Impacts of producing goods
card: Making goods uses resources. These include land for farms and factories, water, energy and raw materials such as timber, metals and cotton.
Using these resources can reduce what is left for other people and for nature. Water taken for a factory, for example, is no longer in the river.
Production can cause pollution. A factory may release smoke into the air, or waste into rivers and soil.
Clearing land for a farm, mine or factory can destroy habitat, the place where plants and animals live. Animals that lose their habitat may die or have to move.
draft.remember: Making goods uses resources and can pollute air, water and land or destroy habitat.

a.q: A company clears a forest to build a cotton farm. Which impact of production does this show?
opts: Habitat loss where the farm is built
Waste thrown away by people who buy cotton
Pollution from clothes sent to landfill
Fair pay for the workers on the farm
a.why: Clearing the forest removes the place where plants and animals live, which is habitat loss. Waste from buyers is an effect of using goods, not of making them.
a.clue: Think about what happens to the animals that lived in the forest.

b.q: A factory in a river town makes paper and lets waste water run into the river. Which impact of production does this cause?
opts: Water pollution that can harm river life
Habitat loss from clearing land for the farm
Less energy used to make the paper
b.why: Waste water entering the river is pollution, and it can harm the fish and plants living there. Habitat loss is about clearing land, which this case does not describe.
b.clue: Look at where the waste from the factory ends up.

a.best: Habitat loss where the farm is built

b.best: Water pollution that can harm river life
